verdicts.note: H1N1 vaccination uptake among pregnant women.
No abstract; decline in co-residence of parents and children among OLDER Kuwaitis. The homonym.
No abstract; 'Social norms, partnerships and children' in a household-economics journal could sit on either side of Wall 3.
Review of 'The Stem Family in Eurasian Perspective'. The comparative stem-family literature that underpins the extended arm's historical half.
Grandparent roles in Japan and Singapore against a DECLINE IN THREE-GENERATIONAL HOUSEHOLDS driven by low fertility. Exposure trend, and the reverse arrow is explicit in the framing.

Timing and SEQUENCING of first sex, marriage, BIRTH and INDEPENDENT HOUSING in two Nairobi informal settlements. All four markers in one retrospective survey, in a sub-Saharan setting the frame is thin on.
Marriage decision-making and reproductive health among married youth in Pakistan.
No abstract; intergenerational support of the elderly in Iran.
No abstract; parenthood and happiness review.
Kinship, altruism and gender disparities in education; residence rules enter as a monitoring-cost premise, education is the outcome.
Intra-household allocation of South African social grants.
No abstract; 'Nest Leaving in Europe' is squarely link 1 but the outcome is not visible.
Early-life socioeconomic adversity and adult biomarkers.

CHANGING DETERMINANTS of UK young adults' living arrangements, with more now remaining in the parental home despite an early average age at leaving. A within-country trend in the exposure with determinants estimated -- the shape Wall 3 wants, missing only the birth.
Grandparental INVESTMENT and reproductive decisions in the 1970 British cohort. Reclassified at the anchor gate: the exposure is kin investment, not the arrangement, so C.2.a's.
No abstract; social integration and life satisfaction of childless adults.
Whether shrinking cohort size improves life chances. C.6.a's Easterlin question.
Household structure in early modern Italian cadastres; historical description.
Children's independent walking in Great Britain.
Non-marital births in Romania from the GGS.
Parenthood among people with intellectual disabilities.
Book review of Understanding Chinese Families.
Reference entry titled 'Marriage', no abstract.
Reference entry titled 'Demography', no abstract.
Reference entry titled 'Marital Rights', no abstract.
UK childhood demography statistics.

Union formation among young women in SPAIN, against a lengthening stay in the parental home and the rise of PARTNERSHIPS WITHOUT CO-RESIDENCE. The registered setting, and it names the living-apart-together configuration that batch 5 flagged.
Life-course event timing in sparsely populated versus urban Sweden for the 1968-71 cohort, and how timing shapes later residential choice. C.2.g seam.
Korean volume on the socioeconomic impacts of low fertility and ageing.
Age identity among college students.

PATRILOCAL RESIDENCE against MARITAL FERTILITY in contemporary China, testing the traditional link between residence and early high fertility against a period of rapid decline. A direct arrangement-to-fertility estimate in the extended arm's largest setting.

Mexican transitions to adulthood, splitting SOCIAL transitions (schooling, labour entry, PARENTAL HOME LEAVING) from FAMILY FORMATION transitions. The two links separated by design; Latin American setting.
Demographic characteristics of families in the Jordanian Badia.
Socioeconomic determinants of Thai infant growth; 'living with parents' is a covariate for the infant.
No abstract in this record, but this is the gated anchor 'Grandparenting and Childbearing in the Extended Family'. Primary-cell record; the design is not visible from the title alone.
Latent classes of social role configurations in early adulthood against wellbeing.
Aboriginal fathers and children's wellbeing.
Biography review; 'left his impoverished parents' is narrative.

Intergenerational co-residence of YOUNG MARRIED WOMEN across Korea, Japan and China, separating co-residence with natal parents from with parents-in-law -- a distinction §6's configuration split needs and most records collapse. Outcome is the arrangement.
'Doing the month' postpartum practices and Chinese women's health. The confinement month is normally spent in a parental household; outcome is maternal health.
Living arrangement preferences of elderly people in Taiwan.
Parenthood and resistance to the common cold.
Women's trajectories after acute health crisis in Burkina Faso.
Residential PROXIMITY of the nearest child and support receipt among older Barbadians. Proximity as exposure, elder support as outcome.
No abstract; 'A Sudden Transition: Household Changes for Middle Aged U.S. Women in the Twentieth Century' is the parents'-side exposure trend but nothing more is visible.

Fertility INTENTIONS against current intergenerational family relationships and childhood parental divorce, opening by noting that the influence of the parental home on fertility is well established but the MECHANISM is unclear. That is the chapter's own question, asked directly, with a pre-determined childhood exposure. Priority read.
No abstract; economic development and traditional elder support in China.
Fifty years of French census family situations via IPUMS. Exposure trend with a long series and micro-data access.
Cross-border assisted reproduction from India to Dubai. A.17's.

MULTIGENERATIONAL HOUSEHOLDS and the school readiness of children born to unmarried mothers, framed as a policy alternative to marriage promotion. Arrangement as exposure, child development as outcome.
Informal caregiving patterns in Korea and Europe.
Long-term care insurance puzzle.
Social determinants of mortality from childhood to early adulthood.
Intergenerational care for and BY older people in Thailand, including grandparental care of young children. Both directions described; no fertility outcome.

No abstract; 'How far do children move? Spatial distances after leaving the parental home' is the link between home-leaving and the PROXIMITY cell -- the record that would say whether leaving home and living near parents are the same treatment.
